french_characters.name: Émile Driant
french_characters.background: Former deputy, son-in-law of Gen. Boulanger. Author of military fiction under pseudonym 'Capitaine Danrit'. Warned French high command of German preparations in 1915—ignored.
french_characters.physical: Gray-haired, mustached, wiry build. Wore chasseur uniform with Alpine beret.
french_characters.personality: Stoic, methodical, beloved by men. Fatalistic but duty-bound. Intellectual soldier.
french_characters.fate: Killed in action February 22, 1916, Bois des Caures. Shot in head leading counterattack. Body recovered by Germans, buried with honors.
french_characters.last_words: Continue firing. I go to the ravine. Goodbye.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Opening protagonist—dies heroically establishing tone of futility and sacrifice
relationships: Respected by German officers who buried him
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Exact last words documented.

french_characters.name: Henri Moreau
french_characters.background: Law student, mobilized 1914. Wounded at Marne, returned 1915. Protégé of Col. Driant.
french_characters.physical: Dark-haired, thin, intelligent eyes. Scarred left shoulder from Marne wound.
french_characters.personality: Idealistic but increasingly disillusioned. Keeps meticulous diary. Questions the war but fights loyally.
french_characters.fate: Survives Bois des Caures (wounded). Fights through June. Shell-shock during Thiaumont. Evacuated July. Returns October counteroffensive. Survives war.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Witness character—spans entire battle. Eyes of observing player/narrator.
diary_entries: October 25 - 'Douaumont is ours again. We are ghosts claiming ruins.'
french_characters.psychological_state: Progressive descent into dissociation, then hollow resilience
french_characters.historical_note: Composite fictional character based on chasseur memoirs

french_characters.name: Marcel Renard
french_characters.background: Factory worker. Wife and daughter in occupied Lille—no contact since 1914. Fights with quiet desperation.
french_characters.physical: Stocky, strong hands, broken nose. Missing left earlobe (frostbite 1914).
french_characters.personality: Gruff exterior, protective of younger soldiers. Superstitious. Carries daughter's ribbon.
french_characters.fate: Killed June 4, 1916, assault on Fort Vaux. Shot in throat during trench charge.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Everyman soldier—represents working-class poilu. Death is meaningless, abrupt.
french_characters.personal_item: Blue ribbon from daughter Céleste, age 7 (in 1914)
french_characters.last_thoughts: Wonders if Céleste remembers his face
french_characters.historical_note: Fictional but representative of ~50% of French Army (industrial workers)

french_characters.name: Alphonse Dulac
french_characters.background: Career NCO. Veteran of Morocco (1912). Professional soldier, pre-war regular.
french_characters.physical: Tall, lean, scarred hands. Weathered face. Steady eyes.
french_characters.personality: Calm under fire. Cynical about officers, loyal to men. Dark humor. Competent survivor.
french_characters.fate: Survives Verdun. Wounded three times (minor). Transferred October 1916. Survives war.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Veteran archetype—provides continuity and tactical grounding.
french_characters.philosophy: 'War is a job. Do it well or die badly.'
french_characters.historical_note: Composite of career NCO memoirs

french_characters.name: Théodore Beaumont
french_characters.background: Apprentice printer. Mobilized January 1916. Arrived Verdun February 23.
french_characters.physical: Boyish, freckled, red hair. Slight build.
french_characters.personality: Terrified but hides it with nervous chatter. Clings to older soldiers. Wants to prove himself.
french_characters.fate: Killed March 8, 1916, Mort-Homme. Buried alive in collapsed trench during bombardment. Body never recovered.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Innocent lost—represents youth sacrificed. Death is random, suffocating.
relationships: Writes daily to mother (letters found in dugout)
french_characters.last_letter: March 7, 1916—'Maman, we are holding the line. I am not afraid.' (Lie)
french_characters.historical_note: Fictional. Based on age demographics—60,000+ French soldiers age 18-20 at Verdun.

french_characters.name: Jean-Baptiste Fournier
french_characters.background: Colonial soldier, career military. 15 years service in Morocco, Senegal, Indochina.
french_characters.physical: Dark-skinned, powerful build, graying temples. Tribal scars on left cheek (Wolof tradition).
french_characters.personality: Reserved, observant. Feels kinship with Moroccan tirailleurs. Skeptical of European war.
french_characters.fate: Survives October 24 assault on Douaumont. Wounded (bayonet to thigh). Evacuated, survives war. Returns to Martinique 1919.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Outsider perspective—colonial subject fighting for empire. Questions loyalty vs. duty.
french_characters.internal_conflict: 'I fight for a France that does not see me as French.'
french_characters.historical_note: Represents ~600,000 colonial soldiers in French Army WWI. Composite character.

french_characters.name: Régis de Vibraye
french_characters.background: Saint-Cyr military academy graduate. Colonial service. Led RICM at Douaumont recapture.
french_characters.physical: Elegant bearing, dark mustache, hawkish features. Wears kepis with panache.
french_characters.personality: Bold, charismatic, aggressive. Believes in élan (offensive spirit). Cares for men but spends them freely.
french_characters.fate: Survives Verdun. Killed 1917, Chemin des Dames offensive.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Romantic warrior—embodies fading aristocratic military ethos. Success at Verdun reinforces fatal overconfidence.
french_characters.famous_order: October 24—'Moroccan Division will take Douaumont before nightfall. There is no alternative.'
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. RICM did capture Douaumont Oct 24, 1916.

french_characters.name: Sylvain-Eugène Raynal
french_characters.background: Career officer. Assumed command Fort Vaux May 1916 during German encirclement.
french_characters.physical: Stocky, balding, thick mustache. Stoic expression.
french_characters.personality: Dutiful, methodical, unflappable. Inspires by example. No illusions about fate.
french_characters.fate: Surrendered Fort Vaux June 7, 1916 (water exhausted, garrison dying of thirst). German General Falkenhayn allowed him to keep sword. Imprisoned in Germany. Repatriated 1918. Légion d'honneur.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Stoic defender—honor in resistance, not victory. Symbol of endurance.
french_characters.famous_act: Sent final message via carrier pigeon Vaillant, June 4: 'We are holding. Thirst unbearable. Relief urgent.'
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Events documented.

french_characters.name: André Pézard
french_characters.background: Normalien (École Normale Supérieure). Classicist, translator. Mobilized 1914.
french_characters.physical: Thin, bookish, wire-rimmed glasses (broken, taped). Ink-stained fingers.
french_characters.personality: Intellectual observer. Keeps literary journal. Compares Verdun to Dante's Inferno.
french_characters.fate: Severely wounded July 1916 (shrapnel to face and chest). Months of surgery. Survives. Post-war becomes Dante scholar.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Witness-as-artist. Transforms trauma into literature.
relationships: Corresponds with poet friend Jean Cocteau
journal_entries: March 30—'We are not men. We are mud that screams.'
June 12—'Hell is not fire. It is waiting.'
french_characters.post_war: Published memoir 'Nous autres à Vauquois' (We Others at Vauquois, 1918). Translated Dante's Divine Comedy.
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Actual Verdun veteran and post-war Dante translator.

french_characters.name: Louis Pergaud
french_characters.background: Prize-winning novelist ('La Guerre des boutons', 1912). Mobilized 1914.
french_characters.physical: Medium height, dark curly hair, expressive eyes.
french_characters.personality: Sensitive, humane. Wrote about children's innocence pre-war. War destroys his optimism.
french_characters.fate: Killed April 8, 1915 (before Verdun) at Marchéville. Body never found. Listed missing.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Ghost presence—letters and reputation haunt characters. Represents lost generation of artists.
relationships: Known to literate soldiers via his novel
Name invoked as symbol of waste
french_characters.legacy: His novel about children's mock war becomes bitter irony in real war.
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Author killed WWI. Included as cultural reference point.

french_characters.name: Guillaume Apollinaire
french_characters.background: Avant-garde poet, Cubist circle. Naturalized French 1914. Volunteered for army.
french_characters.physical: Rotund, jovial face, bandaged head (shrapnel wound March 1916).
french_characters.personality: Paradoxical—loves war's modernity, horrified by slaughter. Writes surreal poetry in trenches.
french_characters.fate: Wounded by shrapnel, Verdun sector, March 17, 1916. Trepanation surgery. Survives Verdun. Dies Spanish flu 1918.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Artist seduced then repelled by war. Poetry as coping mechanism.
relationships: Admired by soldiers for cheerfulness under fire
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Actually wounded near Verdun.

french_characters.name: Maurice Genevoix
french_characters.background: École Normale Supérieure. Severely wounded 1915 (Éparges). Not at Verdun but emblematic.
french_characters.physical: Wounded left arm (permanent damage).
french_characters.personality: Observer-writer. Sensitive to soldiers' humanity.
french_characters.fate: Survived WWI. Became major author ('Ceux de 14'). Entered Panthéon 2020.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Cultural memory keeper—represents those who testified.
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Not at Verdun but included as literary witness to broader WWI experience.

french_characters.name: Charles Mangin
french_characters.background: Colonial wars veteran (Sudan, Morocco). Controversial for using colonial troops in high-casualty assaults.
french_characters.physical: Bald, intense stare, square jaw. Immaculate uniform.
french_characters.personality: Ruthless, brilliant tactician. 'Victory justifies casualties.' Nicknamed 'the Butcher.'
french_characters.fate: Survives WWI. Commands in Rhineland occupation. Dies 1925.
french_characters.narrative_arc: The general—distant, calculating. Represents command's cold arithmetic.
relationships: Uses colonial troops (FR006, FR007 under his command)
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Commanded October counteroffensive.

french_characters.name: Robert Nivelle
french_characters.background: Artillery specialist. Replaced Pétain May 1916. Doctrine: relentless counterattack.
french_characters.physical: White mustache, ramrod posture, commanding voice.
french_characters.personality: Confident, aggressive, inspiring speaker. Overestimates offensive power.
french_characters.fate: Promoted Commander-in-Chief Dec 1916. 1917 Nivelle Offensive disaster. Removed from command. Survives war.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Tragic overreacher—success at Verdun leads to catastrophic 1917 failure.
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Verdun success misled him into 1917 disaster.

french_characters.name: Philippe Pétain
french_characters.background: Career officer, nearly retired pre-war. Defensive doctrine advocate.
french_characters.physical: Tall, white mustache, cold blue eyes, impassive face.
french_characters.personality: Methodical, cautious, cares for soldiers' welfare. Aloof. Calculating.
french_characters.fate: National hero post-Verdun. Marshal of France. Later: Vichy collaborator WWII. Died in prison 1951.
french_characters.narrative_arc: The savior—but arc extends beyond game into historical tragedy.
relationships: Respected by soldiers ('He rotates us out')
french_characters.famous_order: 'Courage! On les aura!' ('Courage! We'll get them!')
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Complex legacy: WWI hero, WWII traitor.

french_characters.name: Julien Benda
french_characters.background: Philosopher, essayist. Criticizes war intellectuals who glorify violence.
french_characters.physical: Balding, bespectacled, scholarly appearance.
french_characters.personality: Rational, critical, morally opposed to war fervor. Observes from distance.
french_characters.fate: Survives war. Writes 'La Trahison des Clercs' (1927) condemning intellectual war support.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Conscience voice—contrast to front-line characters.
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Included for intellectual context.

french_characters.name: Madeleine Clemenceau-Jacquemaire
french_characters.background: Sculptor, daughter of politician Georges Clemenceau. Documented war through art.
french_characters.physical: Strong-featured, intense gaze, artist's hands.
french_characters.personality: Determined, defiant of gender norms. Seeks truth in suffering.
french_characters.fate: Survives war. Sculpts war memorials.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Observer-as-artist (female perspective).
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. WWI sculptor.

french_characters.name: Jean Bernier
french_characters.background: Teacher. Mobilized 1914. Wounded twice. Becomes pacifist.
french_characters.physical: Thin, haunted eyes, nervous hands.
french_characters.personality: Idealist turned radical pacifist. Hides anti-war views from officers.
french_characters.fate: Survives Verdun. Participates in 1917 mutinies (minor role). Survives war. Joins anti-war movements.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Disillusionment arc—from patriot to refusenik.
relationships: Secret pacifist writings shared among soldiers
french_characters.historical_note: Composite character. Represents pre-1917 mutiny sentiment.

french_characters.name: Ahmed ben Mokhtar
french_characters.background: Algerian tirailleur (colonial infantry). Conscripted 1914.
french_characters.physical: Dark-skinned, lean, scarred left hand (childhood burn).
french_characters.personality: Quiet, observant. Faithful Muslim. Prays five times daily when possible. Skeptical of French promises.
french_characters.fate: Killed June 19, 1916, gas attack near Fleury. Buried in Muslim section, Douaumont Cemetery.
french_characters.narrative_arc: Colonial subject—fights for empire that marginalizes him.
french_characters.internal_thought: 'They call us brothers in the trenches. Will they call us brothers in Paris?'
french_characters.historical_note: Composite. ~173,000 Algerian soldiers served France WWI.

french_characters.name: Lucien Laby
french_characters.background: Postal worker. Meticulous record-keeper. Keeps daily war diary.
french_characters.physical: Average height, brown hair, small hands (writer's hands).
french_characters.personality: Obsessive documenter. Believes recording truth is duty to dead.
french_characters.fate: Survives Verdun. Survives war. Publishes diary 'Les Carnets de l'aspirant Laby' (1935).
french_characters.narrative_arc: Chronicler—records for posterity.
french_characters.diary_style: Precise, unadorned. Lists dead by name daily.
french_characters.historical_note: Real person. Actual WWI diarist.
